title: I've been making a UI Overhaul Mod for an AI game called Idelworlds and I'm having the most fun with development than I've had in decades.
author: MrCyberthief
selftext:
*This isn't intended to be self promotion or even promotion of the game at all, but I've marked it that way to be safe.*

Alright so... I have a Bachelors Degree in game development, I did it while i was in my 20s and after I finished it I fell out of love with game dev. I was good at my job, I was a 3D art guy mostly.  
As passionate as I was, it just didn't pay the bills and work was too sparse and unreliable. 

In late April, I started playing Idleworlds (idleworlds.com) by Matduke, I used to listen to his music as a teenager and knew him from the Going Quantum Podcast and Monstercat media, so when i saw his reddit ad pop up i jumped in and gave it a go.

Immediately I could tell it was fully vibe coded but that didnt bother me, it was brand new and only had about 30 or 40 players. 

Over the past few months, I found a need for tools not available in the game, things like gear planners and calculators so i started off scripting small, easy to use tools in Excel.   
I was really enjoying it, getting back into coding and started playing around with other tools before making the switch to a hybrid AI/Self-coded venture with Claude to speed things up. 

Well... it was a blast. I shared my tool and people loved it, and as the player base exploded it got more and more popular. This was the first spark.  
You can check out my toolkit here [https://idleworldstoolkit.com/](https://idleworldstoolkit.com/)  
  
Eventually I had gotten the toolkit to a place I was happy with, so i started working on something new.  
**I started working on a full reskin.**   
  
It was my first "fully" vibe coded venture and I trained the AI on art that i'd made previously for D&D campaigns and stuff. I tried my hardest to keep it as honest as I can.   
I did jump in and do a lot of manual editing of assets, extensive photoshop and illustrator work... etc. all the standard stuff.

This went about as well as expected - For me it was a constant struggle to keep up with game updates, new skills, new menus etc because that guy worked FAST.   
Being a fully vibe coded game, patches were frequent, but I kept it up and the pace became a fun challenge for me. 

Today, my reskin project is live and it makes the game look incredible. So much so, that the developer helped me implement it as an official in-game theme and im so invested.  
*He offered to compensate me for it and i declined.* 

My love for development has been reignited in a way I least expected.

I just wanted to share how AI helped make dev feel exciting again.   
I'm getting back into animating, coding etc just like before (by hand and with Agents), and having a blast.

I'd love to hear about similar stories, im sure they're abundant here!
